obligations.note: Commit 411570a changes required_approvals from `amount >= DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD` to `amount > DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD`, so a payment of exactly 10,000.00 now needs one approver. PAY-1 requires two distinct approvers at or above the approved 10,000.00 threshold, and no exception in the register covers this deviation.

Ledger entry ACR-0401 (exhaustive Rocq proof of `required_approvals = 2 iff a >= threshold`, made on d30b2ad) covers payments.py#required_approvals. This change alters that code's behaviour, so the evidence has lapsed, and no new evidence of the same strength was provided.
Ticket CHG-24576 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-15, before review. Its components payments.payments and payments.tests cover both changed paths.
There is a code_review approval from mara.costa, a payments change_approver who is a different person from the author sofia.santos according to the directory.
The code_review approval names the head commit 411570a56bdc, so it covers what would be merged.

The CI run in records/ci/run.json was on 4655e99, not on head 411570a. The later commit changes behaviour (the dual-control comparison), so that run doesn't count, and there is no passing run of the full suite or of the PAY-1 control test on the final commit.

summary: PR-1442 is described as adding a display helper, but its second commit, 'Simplify threshold check', turns the dual-control comparison from >= into >. A payment of exactly 10,000.00 would then be released with a single approver, which violates PAY-1, and no exception covers it. The earlier exhaustive PAY-1 proof (ACR-0401) has lapsed because the covered code changed, and the only CI run was on the earlier commit, so CHG-4 is not met either. Ticket, independent review and approval-on-head are in order, but the change must be rejected.
